script.opening_words: You built the spreadsheet yourself, which is either impressive or a warning sign, and now you are staring at a row you are pretty sure is a typo. It took you 19 years to save
script.ending_words: no notification and no confetti, it started growing because has existed. The quarter million was never the achievement. The quarter million is just your receipt for surviving the part where it was all on you.
script.analysis: All 18,889 canonical characters read in contiguous 0-11,000 and 11,000-18,889 chunks. A self-built spreadsheet and suspected typo introduce the 19-year versus faster $750K paradox, with a promised nine-second conditional truth line. TIME is defined early. Bernadette saves $500/month, with a year-seven bachelorette-sacrifice scene; Lowell saving $2K/month is a deliberate counterexample. Crossovers and the $125K c/q identity pay the open loop. Coasting is the reward, followed by a comment request and faceless-channel community pitch. Four caveats cover return sequence, valuations/forecasts, inflation and fees. Survey means versus medians and a continuous-saver cohort restore encouragement. The closing spreadsheet/receipt callback validates the grind. Paired cases make algebra accessible; most people quit and most viewers are below the line remain unverified audience/population claims. Return conventions change between monthly contributions and annual coasting. Audio, editing and retention unverified.

claim_audit: The script correctly distinguishes quarter-way in dollars from halfway in TIME. With zero starting wealth, constant positive periodic return q, fixed end-period contribution c, no withdrawals or cost changes and a fixed nominal $1M target, B_n=(c/q)((1+q)^n-1). Equal-duration legs from zero to $250K and $250K to $1M imply x=(1+q)^n=3 and c/q=$125K. This is valid conditional algebra, not a universal market law. Different starting balances, deposit timing or growth, withdrawals, real targets or stochastic returns change the comparison; zero/negative returns need separate treatment.

At quoted annual 7% divided by 12 and end-month deposits, $500/month reaches $250K in 19.5603 years, then $1M after 16.8165 more, broadly matching 19y7m/16y10m. $2K/month gives 7.8462 and 11.7141 more years, broadly 7y10m/11y8m. Bernadette balances at years 3/5/7/10 reproduce $19,965/$35,796/$53,999/$86,542, with $42K deposited by year seven. These are strong conditional scenario calculations, not verified worker outcomes.

The script calls 7% an expected annual return but uses nominal 7%/12 for monthly deposits, effectively 7.229% annually. Its annualized contribution crossover $6K/.07=$85,714 and $8,750/year=$729.17/month line agree with c/q=$125K under that convention. If 7% means EFFECTIVE annual return, monthly q=(1.07)^(1/12)-1 and the equal-time monthly contribution is $706.77; $500/month first reaches $250K in 19.8363 years. Consistent periodic rates are required before calling the annual-rate form exact. Year-end $6K deposits have different crossing times.

Expected growth $250K x .07 = $17,500 is not cash thrown off or assured income. Crossover compares modeled growth with deposits, not labor earnings or an irreversible handoff. Negative returns can make a past crossover recede. Saving remains a lever afterward; fees, allocation, taxes and time matter beforehand. Most viewers contributing under $729/month is unsupported without audience data.

No-deposit doublings use EFFECTIVE annual rates: log(4)/log(1.07) = 20.4895 years; 8% gives 18.0129; 10% gives 14.5451; 6% gives 23.7913. These broadly match the narration but switch convention from the monthly-rate contribution model. At 7%/12 monthly, coasting instead takes 19.862 years. Late-30s to late-50s millionaire status is conditional nominal compounding with no withdrawals, not guaranteed retirement income. Bernadette starting at 31 and saving nearly 20 years would coast from about 51 to 71. A target-date fund changes allocation and is not identical to 100% S&P 500.

Dimensional supports the S&P 500 -0.95% annualized total return for January 2000-December 2009. $1M x .9905^10 = $908,960 reproduces $909K. That is nominal time-weighted index history, not every investor cash-flow outcome. The claim that this decade barely dents her first ten years and improves year 30 lacks the ordered return/deposit path and counterfactual. Buying lower can help if recovery follows, not automatically. A later 5-10-year delay also needs explicit paths.

Vanguard 2026 outlook PDF pages 4 and 17 gives 4%-5% average U.S. stock returns over 5-10 years, as of September 30, 2025, rather than the narrated 4%-6%. Goldman October 2024 primary forecast of 3% through 2034 is a different dated model, not a fresh 2026 forecast. Neither establishes a current four-firm consensus. Exact recording-date CAPE 42, historical ranking and only five calendar years between 8%-12% remain unverified without a dated series and index/dividend definition. Nobody forecasts seven is too absolute; a target-date mix is not interchangeable with a U.S. equity forecast.

At 5%/12 monthly, $500/month takes 22.5671 years to $250K, then 22.1977 more to $1M, close to 22.5/22.2. The nominal line $125K x .05/12 = $520.83 and annual crossover $6K/.05 = $120K reproduce. Purchasing power $1M/1.025^20 = $610,271 and $1M/1.03^20 = $553,676 reproduces $610K/$554K. Steady inflation is assumed. The title keeps a nominal $1M target; a real inflation-indexed target moves.

The fee example simplifies 7% to 6% by subtracting one percentage point. A 1% charge after 7% growth instead gives 1.07 x .99 = 1.0593. Fee timing matters. Stored instead of 300s is ambiguous ASR and is not silently repaired to .03%. The approximately three-year-four-month delay requires specified rate/fee conventions. Plan participants do not entirely control every available fee; advice benefits and other costs are unmeasured.

SCF 2022 median family net worth $192,900 and mean $1,063,700 support a 5.5143 ratio in 2022 dollars. They do not establish any individual under $200K is middle regardless of age, nor show most of every neighbor wealth is home equity. Retirement accounts omit housing and can be pre-tax. Provider means/medians do not place half of all Americans at that account balance. Fidelity $141K/$32,800 and the $558,300 continuous-saver cohort need matched historical releases. Q4 2025 mean $146,400 differs but does not refute older figures. Continuous employment/saving selects survivors and contribution/employer patterns; it does not causally prove persistence alone.

Vanguard How America Saves 2026 original PDF page 6 gives mean $167,970 and median $44,115, supporting rounded $168K/$44K. Pages 8 and 98 show 6% hardship use among participants where offered in 2025; page 99 gives foreclosure/eviction 36% and medical 31%, supporting the leading reasons. These refer to the provider sample, not all Americans. Narrated 4.6% of households with $1M retirement assets, 9.2% at age 55-64, median $500/month saving and most quitting years 3-7 lack matched weighted sources and cannot be inferred from Bernadette.

Munger $100K to $222K inflation conversion needs an authenticated date and CPI observation; full-year 2026 inflation is unavailable. The faceless YouTube community as fastest contribution-growth route is promotional opinion without comparative earnings, costs or success data. Retirement balances are not after-tax cash; early access and distribution taxes matter. No withdrawal-rate guarantee is expressly modeled here, and reaching $1M does not prove retirement adequacy. A disclaimer does not validate projections.
